title: Blind composition duels · Note Duel
excerpt: A blind listening study of AI-composed music
content_html:
A blind listening study of AI-composed music

Two pieces. One brief. You decide.

Hear two compositions written for the same brief, labelled only A and B. Pick the better music. Then we show you who wrote what, and how everyone else voted.

About a minute per duel · no sign-up · headphones help

0votes cast

0full-listen votes

0listeners

0/76duels you've judged

How a duel works

  1. 1

    Listen blind

    Both pieces play through the same engraver and synthesizer at matched loudness. Sides are shuffled for every listener.

  2. 2

    Vote

    A, B, tie, or neither. Add why if you like. Hearing both in full makes your vote count in the headline standings.

  3. 3

    Reveal

    See which piece was which, whether it met the brief, and how the crowd split.

Pick a brief

Every model answered the same 5 briefs. Choose one, or press Start a duel and we'll pick the pairing that needs votes most.

  • Minuet in G major Piano · G major · 3/4 · 16 bars Write a graceful minuet for solo piano in the galant style. 0/15 judged Listen
  • Two-voice invention in D minor Piano · D minor · 4/4 · 12 bars Write a two-voice invention for piano in the manner of Bach. 0/21 judged Listen
  • Nocturne in E-flat major Piano · E-flat major · 4/4 · 8 bars Write a short romantic nocturne for piano. 0/15 judged Listen
  • Toy soldier march in C major Piano · C major · 2/4 · 16 bars Write a bright, witty march for piano. 0/15 judged Listen
  • Modal miniature in D Dorian, 5/4 Piano · D Dorian · 5/4 · 8 bars Write a contemporary miniature for piano in D Dorian and 5/4 time. 0/10 judged Listen

Built to be fair

Blind & shuffled

Titles and sources stay hidden until you vote. Each listener gets a random A/B placement, fixed on reload.

Same instrument, same volume

Every score is engraved and synthesized by one pipeline and loudness-matched, so production can't win the vote.

Full listens count

A vote counts as a full listen only if you heard at least 90% of both pieces. Partial listens are kept, but apart.

Uncertainty, always

Rankings use a Bradley–Terry model with 95% bootstrap intervals and rank ranges, and stay provisional under 30 judgments.

Per-task results

Every brief's head-to-head is published on its own, so one overall number never hides where a piece won.

Neither ≠ tie

“Both equal” and “neither is good” are different answers. Rejections are reported separately rather than mixed into the ranking.
